value.rationale: The first-difference Stein factor is a naturally required coefficient in total-variation distribution approximation. The theorem optimizes an exact known but unevaluated envelope throughout all positive log-concave constant-birth laws, resolves a recent explicitly posed sharp-factor problem, identifies all extremal lattice indices and produces the exact finite-parameter Bessel improvement from a loose 3/w bound. Its nonnegative gap is a structural stability formula, not a random parameter slice or numerical table recomputation.
